subsystems.name: Neural interface
subsystems.role: the hardware that writes signals into the brain at the resolution of small groups of neurons, and ideally reads back what happens.

subsystems.name: Encoding model
subsystems.role: a mathematical map from stimulation patterns to the experience the person reports.

subsystems.name: Stimulation engine
subsystems.role: delivers precisely timed, spatially patterned pulses rather than a blanket current.

subsystems.name: Readout and feedback
subsystems.role: measures the resulting brain activity and the person's own report, so the model can be corrected.

subsystems.name: Safety layer
subsystems.role: keeps stimulation within limits that do not damage tissue, and makes effects reversible.

buildSteps.title: Choose a natural sense to copy
buildSteps.detail: Start with a sense whose neural code is best understood, because you must first reproduce a known experience before inventing an unknown one.

buildSteps.title: Record the real thing
buildSteps.detail: Measure brain activity while a person sees, hears or touches, building a dataset linking physical input to neural patterns.

buildSteps.title: Model the code
buildSteps.detail: Fit a model that predicts the pattern from the stimulus — the first half of any write path.

buildSteps.title: Build a writer
buildSteps.detail: Develop an implant that can inject activity into the same population of neurons, at the right places and times, without damaging tissue.

buildSteps.title: Reproduce a known sensation
buildSteps.detail: Drive the model in reverse and check the person reports roughly the experience you aimed for; simple flashes of light from cortical stimulation are the closest existing evidence that this is possible.

buildSteps.title: Search beyond nature
buildSteps.detail: Once you can write a known pattern, vary it in ways that no real sense organ produces and see what, if anything, is experienced.

buildSteps.title: Close the loop
buildSteps.detail: Let the person's reports and the recorded brain activity retrain the model, so it converges on patterns that actually produce stable, describable experiences.

buildSteps.title: Prove it is safe and reversible
buildSteps.detail: Demonstrate years of stable operation with no tissue damage and a reliable way to stop or remove the effect.

prerequisites.why: electrode arrays can read and stimulate cortex, but not yet with nanoscale precision across large areas, and implants degrade over years.
these give cell-type-specific control in animals and are the closest tool to writing arbitrary patterns, but are not yet usable in people.
much is known about vision and touch, very little about how complex or emotional experience is encoded.

prerequisites.tech: A scientific account linking brain activity to subjective experience
prerequisites.why: without it there is no way to verify that a written pattern produces the experience intended, or any at all.
materials that survive decades inside the brain without scarring or immune reaction do not yet exist at the needed scale.

pathway.milestone: cortical stimulation that evokes simple sensations such as phosphenes, plus sensory-substitution devices that route one sense through another
pathway.unlocks: proof that injected activity is experienced as something.

pathway.milestone: implants that restore a lost sense, such as a visual prosthesis stable enough for daily use
pathway.unlocks: a validated write path into human cortex, with years of safety data.

pathway.milestone: experiences that have no natural trigger but are still describable — for example a direct perception of a magnetic or ultrasonic field
pathway.unlocks: evidence that the brain can host signals evolution never gave it.
